prerequisites: It is recommended to first acquire the knowledge foreseen in the course of Technical Physics and Elements of Heat Transfer.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the basic knowledge to navigate the complex world of hospital systems.
Deepen the topics of air conditioning, analyzing all elements from the heating/cooling plant to the system terminals.
Consider the distribution of heat transfer fluids and, in the case of air distribution networks, focus on the problem of filtration, air quality, and air distribution within the premises.
Analyze the most common technical solutions in the hospital sector, considering the relevant regulatory framework.
Knowledge of technical systems present in clinical settings, particularly the role of air conditioning systems as complex systems and the problems encountered in their management and design.
Identify the best technological solutions suitable for the specific case.
Identify and compare different technological solutions to meet the requirements and objectives to be achieved in the project.
Collaborate within a working group, defining objectives, activities, and tools.
Reflect on the knowledge and skills of one's educational path, identify possibilities for further development of knowledge, abilities, and competences.

syllabus_topics: Concepts of well-being and comfort indices, PMV and PPD
Local discomfort and notes on adaptive comfort
Air filtration and Indoor Air Quality
Description of the main air conditioning systems serving buildings
Air conditioning systems: Generalities: autonomous and centralized systems, direct and with heat transfer fluid; description of heating/cooling system components: heating terminals
Generalities on air handling units and notes on thermal load
Mixed air-water systems in summer and winter mode
Air distribution and its movement within rooms
Air movement in environments and infection control in healthcare settings
teaching_methods: Site visits to technical rooms hosting university air conditioning systems
assessment_rules: The assessment will consist of an oral colloquium where the student will be evaluated by answering three or more questions regarding air conditioning systems, air quality and/or comfort, and hospital technical systems. The exam will be passed if the student demonstrates sufficient knowledge regarding the required questions. Students with disabilities or specific learning disorders may agree on alternative examination methods with the instructor.
